sees.anonymous: the landing page and an empty public hackathon list; a “Log in” button

title: logs in to the platform
comment: Signs in through Keycloak; the session is what identifies them and their role on every step below.

title: admin creates and publishes the hackathon
page: /hackathons/create — fill name, dates, visibility, main image
provides: name, description rich markdown (tables, youtube embeded videos, images), visibility, main image, startsAt, endsAt
comment: Creates the event and returns the hackathonId every later step targets. Logo is an image url.

title: admin confirms the event is published
comment: Reads the event back to confirm name, description and image URL were stored.

at: the event is created and public

sees.anonymous: the public event page — name, description, logo
sees.admin1: the full manage hub for the new event (config, timeline, participants, teams, prizes)

title: admin builds the custom registration form
provides: Affiliation (text, required); Experience level (select, required); Skills (tags); Why do you want to take part? (textarea, required); Dietary requirements (text); T-shirt size (select); I accept the Code of Conduct (consent, required); I consent to event photography (consent)
comment: The admin composes a CUSTOM registration questionnaire — each question carries a label, a type (short text, single-choice, tags, or long text) and whether it is required. Here: Affiliation (text, required), Experience level (single-choice), Skills (tags), a free-text Motivation (required), Dietary needs, and T-shirt size (single-choice), plus two consent checkboxes (Code of Conduct required, photos optional). Participants answer exactly these on their registration form.

title: admin builds the custom submission form
provides: Repository URL (url, required); Live demo URL (url); One-paragraph summary (textarea, required); Primary category (select, required); Slides (PDF) — upload or link (file-or-url)
comment: The admin defines the CUSTOM questionnaire teams answer when they turn work in: Repository URL (required), a Live demo URL, a Summary (long text, required), a Primary category (single-choice, required), and Slides (upload or external link). The submission is validated against exactly these questions.

title: admin sets the voting policy
provides: hackathonId, mechanism, oneBallotPer, ownTeamVoting, organizerVoting, tieBreak
comment: Sets the rules of the vote up front: mechanism, whether own-team votes count, and how ties break.

title: admin sets the email templates
comment: The templates the platform sends at each milestone, written once with placeholders.

title: admin defines the prize table
comment: Records the prize table; the admin has the final say on prizes.

title: admin sets the phases with time windows
provides: hackathonId, registrationOpens, registrationCloses, proposalsClose, preferencesClose, submissionsClos
comment: The clock: when each stage opens and closes. Opened now so registration and proposals can proceed.

title: admin adds the Ideation phase
comment: Lays the timeline: each phase is a named window participants see. Ideation is first.

title: admin adds the Hacking phase
comment: The build window.

title: admin adds the Judging phase
comment: The final window, where voting happens.

title: admin schedules voting to open in the Judging phase
comment: Linking VOTE to the Judging phase means voting opens automatically when that phase becomes current — not before.

title: admin sets the opening capabilities
comment: Register and propose open now; submit, vote and results stay closed until their phases.

title: admin declares the Ideation phase current
comment: Declares which phase is “now” so the hub and participants agree on the current stage.

at: setup complete — registration open, Ideation is current

sees.anonymous: the public event page and the two pre-proposed projects
sees.admin1: everything, plus the Now/Next box showing Ideation
sees.user1: the public event page with a Join button (registration is open)
sees.user2: the public event page with a Join button

title: admin proposes Project1 (preconfigured)
comment: The admin pre-proposes Project1 so the event ships with projects ready — participants prefer and join these rather than proposing their own.

title: admin approves Project1
comment: Approves Project1, making it a real project a team can be built around.

title: admin proposes Project2 (preconfigured)
comment: The admin pre-proposes Project2, so there are two projects to spread the two users across.

title: admin approves Project2
comment: Approves Project2.

title: logs in to the platform
comment: Signs in through Keycloak; the session is what identifies them and their role on every step below.

at: user1 signs in — a platform account now exists
shows: a new row in the platform-wide user list (admin only)

title: user1 registers
comment: user1 registers; waitlisted until the organiser approves.

shows: a new row badged “Waitlisted” in Manage participants (the registration list)

title: admin approves user1
comment: The organiser confirms user1 — approval turns a registrant into a full participant.

title: user1 configures their profile (name, skills, avatar image URL)
comment: user1 fills their platform profile. The avatar is set from an image URL hosted by an EXTERNAL provider — a link, not an upload; the platform stores only the URL.

title: user1 submits the registration form (participation)
comment: user1 answers the admin's custom registration questions (affiliation, experience, skills, motivation, diet, T-shirt) and ticks the required consent; the answers are stored against their participation.

shows: their custom-form answers (affiliation, experience, motivation …) are now on file under their row

title: logs in to the platform
comment: Signs in through Keycloak; the session is what identifies them and their role on every step below.

at: user2 signs in — a platform account now exists
shows: a new row in the platform-wide user list (admin only)

title: user2 registers
comment: user2 registers.

title: admin approves user2
comment: The organiser confirms user2.

title: user2 configures their profile (name, skills, avatar image URL)
comment: user2 fills their profile and sets an avatar from an EXTERNAL image URL (a link to a picture hosted elsewhere).

title: user2 submits the registration form (participation)
comment: user2 answers the same custom questions with their own responses and submits their participation.

at: both users are registered and confirmed participants

sees.anonymous: the public event page (never the member area)
sees.admin1: the participants roster with two confirmed people and their registration answers
sees.user1: the member area — overview, projects, teams, and their own profile; may set preferences
sees.user2: the member area; may set preferences

title: user1 prefers Project1
comment: user1 marks the project they want to work on; organisers use preferences for team matching.

shows: user1's preferred project shows in the organiser's preferences export

title: user2 prefers Project2
comment: user2 marks their preferred project.

title: admin exports preferences for team matching in csv/json
comment: The organiser pulls everyone's preferences to inform how teams are formed.

title: admin creates Team1 on Project1
comment: Team1 is bound to Project1 — a seat the CSV import will fill.

title: admin creates Team2 on Project2
comment: Team2 is bound to Project2.

title: admin defines team membership from an uploaded CSV
comment: The organiser assigns each confirmed participant to a team in bulk: user1 joins Team1, user2 joins Team2. Align the copy strings to the Manage-Teams importer when running for real.

sees.admin1: the teams board with Team1 and Team2 and their members

shows: user1 on Team1 and user2 on Team2 in the teams board / people panel

title: admin advances to the Hacking phase
comment: Moving the marker into Hacking opens the submissions the phase names.

sees.user1: a “Turn in work” control for Team1
sees.user2: a “Turn in work” control for Team2

title: user1 turns in Team1's work
comment: user1 submits Team1's work against Project1.

shows: Team1's submission appears for organisers to review

title: user2 turns in Team2's work
comment: user2 submits Team2's work.

title: admin advances to the Judging phase
comment: Advancing to Judging opens the VOTE capability, which was linked to this phase in setup.

title: admin opens voting
comment: Voting needs BOTH this master switch and the VOTE capability the Judging phase opened; the organiser flips it here.

sees.admin1: the tally as ballots arrive (organisers do not vote)
sees.user1: a ballot to cast (not for their own team)

title: admin creates a vote category
comment: A category is what ballots are cast in; opening voting needs at least one.

title: user1 casts a ballot (for Team2)
comment: user1 votes for the other team's submission — own-team voting is off in this event's policy.

shows: user1's ballot is counted in the tally; ballots are organiser-only to read

title: user2 casts a ballot (for Team1)
comment: user2 votes for the other team.

title: admin records the winner
comment: The admin places the winner from the tally — results are advisory until the admin records them (the admin has the final voice).

title: admin publishes the results
comment: Turning on VIEW_RESULTS is what publishes the placements to participants.

sees.anonymous: the public event page (and published winners, if surfaced there)
sees.user1: the published winner on the results page

title: user1 views the published results
comment: user1 sees the published winner. The event is complete.

title: user2 views the published results
comment: user2 sees the published winner. The event is complete.
